In Support of L.D. 17 6, "An Act to Establish a Regional Ambulance Service in
Southern Penobscot County" Joint Standing Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety
Monday, February 10, 2025

Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and members of the Criminal Justice
and Public Safety Committee. My name is Senator Brad Farrin and I am writing on
behalf of myself and Senator Stacey Guerin in support of L.D. 176, "An Act to Establish
a Regional Ambulance Service in Southern Penobscot County"
The the need for reliable, accessible, and well-coordinated EMS is vital. Our region,
encompassing various rural areas and towns, often faces unique challenges when it comes
to delivering emergency care. Response times, resource limitations, and staffing
shortages can all impact the ability to save lives. By implementing this ambulance
service, this bill will provide the necessary changes needed to address these challenges,
ensuring that emergencies are addressed quickly as possible when every second matters.
This new authority will streamline communication and coordination among EMS
providers, allow for more efficient use of resources, and ultimately improve the quality of
care delivered to residents. It will also provide local responders with the support they need to continue serving their communities without facing the constant strain of limited funding and volunteer shortages.
I believe that the establishment of this Regional Ambulance Service is a necessary step toward ensuring the safety, health, and well-being of all residents in our region. I urge
you to support this bill and help strengthen our EMS system.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Cory Reynolds DEXTER LD 176
March 29, 2025
Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and members of the Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety,
I am writing to express my strong support for LD 176, An Act to Establish a Regional Ambulance Service in Southern Penobscot County. As a concerned citizen, I am deeply troubled by the struggles our Emergency Medical Services (EMS) are facing statewide.
The alarming reality is that people are waiting over 45 minutes for an ambulance, primarily due to staffing shortages. Furthermore, some towns are unable to receive ambulance services from neighboring towns, as evident in Corinth, where the town council voted to restrict ambulance services to only within Corinth. This is unacceptable and highlights the urgent need for a regional ambulance service.
LD 176 aims to address these critical issues by establishing a regional ambulance service in Southern Penobscot County. I firmly believe that this legislation is essential to ensuring timely and reliable emergency medical services for our communities.
I respectfully urge you to vote "ought to pass" on LD 176. This bill has the potential to save lives and alleviate the suffering of those in need. I am confident that, together, we can make a positive impact on the lives of Maine residents.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely, Cory Reynolds

Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, members of the Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety, my name is Joe Kellner of Windham, and I am the chief executive officer of LifeFlight of Maine -- a statewide not-for profit critical care air ambulance service. I have worked in Emergency Medical Services in Maine for over 20 years and have experience with nearly every delivery model of EMS that we have here. In addition, I spent seven years serving on the Board of Emergency Medical Services, including two years as its chair, and participated in both Blue-Ribbon Commission studies on Emergency Medical Services in Maine.

l am very pleased to see this enabling legislation come before the committee, which has potential to
increase the efficiency with which emergency medical services are delivered in southern Penobscot County.
One of the repeating themes in EMS in Maine is the inefficiency with which it is delivered, and the
duplication of overhead structures required to maintain nearly 150 individual transporting services. Each of these services must have a chief, a training officer, a unique quality plan, a billing agency, enrollments with
Medicare and MaineCare, and the list goes on.

By creating a pathway to join, together EMS agencies can leverage a larger scope and scale and enhance the efficiency with which EMS is delivered to a particular region.
While my testimony today is more broad than Penobscot County, it is where I spent years as an EMS
clinician and leader, and l feel compelled to share that the area is filled with great minds and a collaborative attitude, ripe for this type of arrangement.

As you consider this legislation, I would encourage you to think more broadly and consider an alternative approach here. l would take this a step further and eliminate any barrier to the establishment of regionalized ambulance services through deregulating any limitation that currently exists. That services must come before the legislature to accomplish this every time is yet another barrier to the improvement
of the EMS system. In my testimony for LD 245 today, I will also speak toward the issues with Maine's
approach to the essentiality of Emergency Medical Services -- this doesn't fix the problem, but it does
improve the situation.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Testimony ofRep. Kenneth Fredette on L.D. 176, "An Act to Establish a Regional Ambulance Service in
Southern Penobscot County" Joint Standing Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety

February 10, 2025
Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and members of the Criminal Justice
and Public Safety Committee. My name is Representative Kemieth Fredette and I am here to testify in support of LD 176, a bill entitled "An Act to Establish a Regional
Ambulance Service in Southern Penobscot County" .
In my home District 33, including the towns of Newport, Corimia, Plymouth, Etna and
Dixmont, there is great concern on Emergency Ambulance Services.
It is my understanding that Northem Light Health is reducing the number of towns it will service, and other previously existing EMS services are, or may not be, able to respond to
an emergency call in a time that prevents a tragic result.
The towns in Southem Penobscot County, and now some towns in adjacent Somerset
County, have expressed a desire to possibly work together to "regionalize" this critical
service.
Due to low, or non-existent, reimbursement rates for calls, staffing shortages, and the
high costs of capital, regionalization appears like the only means to stave off this crisis.
LD 1'76, is the means for us to begin the Work locally on what "regionalization" might
look like and how it will work.
I understand that legislation may exist to address, to some extent, the issue of structure,
however, this bill currently serves as a means to further those conversations and sense of urgency to bring our towns together for the betterment of our communities.
I look forward to working with you during the work session and I am happy to answer any questions you may have.

Kemieth Wade Fredette
State Representative
District 33 Dixmont, Etna, Newport, Plymouth, Corinna

Northern Light Health member organizations include 10 hospitals located in southern,
central, eastern and northern Maine, nursing facilities, air and ground ambulance, behavioral health, addiction treatment, pharmacy, primary and specialty care practices

Northern Light Medical Transport and Emergency Care provides primary emergency ambulance services in Penobscot, Piscataquis, Somerset, Hancock and Aroostook
counties. We also provide mutual aid in regions of Washington County. I want to thank
Representative Fredette for hosting discussions with Southern Penobscot regional
ambulance providers and for sponsoring this legislation.

Like all ambulance service providers in Maine, we are challenged with critical labor
shortages, increases in the cost of providing services and chronic underpayment for the
emergency care that we provide. While we work collaboratively with our regional
ambulance partners, the system is inherently inefficient with each service provider working independently to sustain services in local communities. This bill provides an important solution to chronic emergency response service challenges.

A regional approach will reduce redundancy by locating resources strategically to allow for best case primary response of ambulances and improved back up responses. This bill would support placing ambulances throughout a response area rather than congregated into any one area. A regional approach allows for a more consistent response plan.

This bill allows each community the opportunity to join this collaborative effort and help
guide the direction of EMS as the landscape changes. Each town that opts in has an equal voice and any town may choose to opt out if the program does not align with their
goals.

This institution is an equal opportunity provider and employer.

northernlighthealth.org

Northern Light Medical Transport provides emergency care to more than 100 towns in
Maine. We have varying collaborative agreements in place as part of those responses. We can see the benefit of aligning response plans with a consistent approach
throughout the newly formed region. ln addition to responding to emergency calls, we
can help support the other aspects of this bill including education of emergency medical personnel and developing protocols, policies and procedures to support high standards
of clinical care.
We ask that you support this important legislation. Thank you.
